newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean grain buyers return to market.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean grain buyers return to market.

text.p: South Korean grain buyers are returning to the market after a month-long summer holiday and seeking more corn and by-products for feed ingredients, traders said on Monday.
A visit by South Korean President Kim Young-sam to Latin America is likely to lead to more purchases of Argentine grain products, and possibly Brazilian soymeal, they said.

Traders said the National Livestock Cooperative Federation (NLCF), which bought 209,500 tonnes of Argentine corn last week, was expected to buy another one or two cargoes of corn form the Latin American country this week.

The Korea Feed Association is expected to seek 35,000 tonnes of feed corn and 15,000 tonnes of feed barley on September 17. Several small buyers are seeking 8,000 tonnes of cottonseed meal and 12,500 tonnes of rapeseed meal on Tuesday.
Local corn buyers, heavy purchasers of U.S. corn, are becoming more interested in Argentine corn because of its attractive prices and quality, traders said.

"Argentine corn is getting more competitive in terms of price and quality. It is currently quoted about $10 lower (per tonne) than that of U.S. origin," a senior official at the National Livestock Cooperative Federation said.
